---
title: "ssoossh host check"
description: "Check that this host's sshd will accept ssoossh certificates."
---

<!-- Generated by genclidocs from the cobra command tree in client/cmd. Do not edit. -->

Reports whether this host's sshd will accept ssoossh certificates. It reads sshd's own effective configuration (sshd -T), so Include order, built-in defaults and, with --user, Match blocks are resolved by sshd itself rather than guessed at. It checks that public key authentication is on; that TrustedUserCAKeys names a readable file holding the CA keys the server signs with; that sshd allows the CA's signature algorithm and the client's certificate types; that an AuthorizedPrincipalsCommand passes sshd's path-safety rule and can read its mapping; and that the clock is synchronized.

Read-only: it changes no file and reloads nothing. The CA keys to compare with come from capubkey when one is pinned, otherwise from the server; when neither is available that one comparison is a warning. Run it as root, since sshd -T reads the host keys. Exits non-zero when any check fails, so configuration management can gate on it.

## Synopsis

```
ssoossh host check [flags] [args]
```

## Options

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--addr` | string |  | source address to apply sshd's Match blocks for |
| `--sshd` | string |  | path to sshd (default: sshd on PATH, then /usr/sbin/sshd) |
| `--user` | string |  | local account to check: applies sshd's Match blocks for it and lists the principals that may log in as it |

## Global options

Inherited from [`ssoossh`](/ssoossh/reference/cli/ssoossh/) and its parents.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-c`, `--config` | string |  | path to the ssoossh config file |
| `--file` | string | `/etc/ssoossh/principals.yaml` | path to the local principal mapping file (YAML: local account -&gt; list of principals) |
| `--server` | string |  | server address including scheme (e.g. "https://example.com") assumes https if omited. |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | count | `0` | trace what the command is doing, to stderr; repeat for more (-v steps, -vv requests and files, -vvv bodies) |
